messages:
alex_p: Observed an odd pattern in prod: ~0.7% of WS sessions become 'ghosted' after a tenant auth refresh. Clients still show 'connected' but no server-side KV cache hits and we get repeated reconnects. Timeline: auth rotation -> client reauth -> server rejects resume with 403 but keeps session lease alive -> console still marks stream as open.

vikram: Can you paste the minimal server log for a single incident?

alex_p: Sure — snippet (redacted):
```
2026-03-19T21:12:03Z INFO incoming_conn tenant=acme session=xxxx lease=active
2026-03-19T21:19:01Z WARN token_rotate tenant=acme old_token=revoked
2026-03-19T21:19:02Z INFO reauth_attempt tenant=acme session=xxxx token=new
2026-03-19T21:19:02Z ERROR resume_reject tenant=acme session=xxxx reason=forbidden code=403
2026-03-19T21:19:05Z INFO lease_alive tenant=acme session=xxxx
```

emma_r: So server keeps lease but refuses resume. That explains double-billing symptoms — client reconnect tries resume, fails, then opens a new stream but old lease still counts toward concurrency/quotas.

luis: Do we have a metric that differentiates 'lease_alive but last_activity > X'? IIRC our console only shows connection count and token age, not lease vs active.

telemetry-bot: metric alert: ws.session_ghost_rate acme=0.72% window=1h 

vikram: Repro steps? Is this specific to token rotation timing + idle timeout?

alex_p: Repro was: establish WS, keep idle ~6m, trigger token rotation for tenant, client runs silent reauth (lib handles), server-side auth check on resume fails because new token maps to a new route (we've moved tenant shard during rotation). The resume request hits different runtime that doesn't know the session lease, so rejects. The original runtime doesn't get an explicit close, just lease TTL.

emma_r: Two immediate mitigations: (A) make resume accept old tokens for a short grace window OR (B) ensure resume is routed by stable session id (not token) until session fully closed. Tradeoffs: A expands acceptance surface; B requires routing table change and sticky-routing feature flag.

luis: Also UX/telemetry fixes: console should show "session routing mismatch" as a reason if resume gets 403, include last-route-id, last-auth-age, and a reconnect_count. Right now console shows "connected" which is lying.

alex_p: Proposed short-term: add console annotation for sessions with lease_alive && resume_reject_count > 0 (golden metric), and a canary rollout of sticky session routing for resume requests only. Long-term: adopt session-bind routing key.

vikram: For the sticky resume canary: implement a middleware that on resume requests checks header `X-Session-Prev-Route: <route>` (client or proxy can attach), and preferentially route to that route for 30s. If route missing, fallback. This avoids accepting old tokens.

emma_r: We should also update SDK client backoff to not immediately open a fresh stream on resume 403. Change flow: on resume 403 -> exponential backoff up to 5s -> attempt full reconnect. That reduces duplicate sessions. Sample client pseudo: 
```
if (resume_failed && code==403) {
  await backoff(0, 500, 1000, 2000);
  try_full_connect();
}
```

deploy-bot: Canary of resume-sticky routing v1 rolled to eu-west-1 at 21:45 UTC (canary id=st-resume-2026-0319-1).

luis: Great. Also add new telemetry labels: `resume_route`, `resume_decision` (accepted|proxy_failed|auth_reject), `console_visible` true/false. That will let support filter quickly.

alex_p: I've opened a ticket: PLATFORM-1256 with patch links and a small patch to console UI to mark ambiguous sessions. Assigning to @vikram and @emma_r for the canary + client SDK change.

vikram: Will pick up canary checks, add integration test that simulates route swap during token rotation.

emma_r: I'll update SDK PR and console annotation. Plan to monitor telemetry for 48h post-canary. :eyes:

telemetry-bot: Canary metrics snapshot (10m): eu-west-1 ghost_rate decreased from 0.72% -> 0.21% after sticky-resume canary.

alex_p: Nice. Follow-ups: confirm billing de-dupe logic for lease TTLs, and add a small postmortem note if ghost_rate spikes.

vikram: Agreed. I'll also add a rollout flag so we can quickly toggle sticky resume if any regressions.
